newsitem.title: UK: Clarke sees no change in wait-and-see EMU stance.
newsitem.headline: Clarke sees no change in wait-and-see EMU stance.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he saw no change in the Conservative government's "wait-and-see" policy on participation in a single European currency.
"I don't believe for one moment that anything of that kind is being contemplated," he told BBC radio's Today programme.
"It simply isn't going to happen, it would be senseless were it to happen," Clarke said.

He had been asked about a Daily Telegraph report that Prime Minister John Major had concluded it would be against Britain's interests to join EMU and that he was trying to persuade Clarke to ditch the "wait-and-see" policy before the election.
"The Daily Telegraph is owned and edited by people who hold extremely anti-European views," Clarke said.
He said he and Major had defended the agreed policy at the Conservative party conference six weeks ago.

"The idea that six weeks later we're all talking about changing it is quite preposterous in my view," Clarke said. "It would be no way to fight an election or present yourself to the country as a governing party."

Clarke, who was speaking from Brussels where he will attend a meeting of European Union finance ministers, reiterated his view that there could be no question of countries outside a single currency being fined under the proposed stability pact.
"The only thing that can come out of Europe so far as those outside a single currency are concerned is non-binding recommendations on policy."
"There isn't any question of any fines on those outside, there never has been," Clarke added.
